Thanks Jordan / Samantha — quick thoughts from commerce: 

1) SKU strategy: Recommend separate SKUs for materially different pricing models. If DataForge tiers differ only by quota/throughput, a single metered SKU with tiered meter dimensions (units consumed) simplifies billing and search. Use separate SKUs only if there are additional entitlements (e.g., premium features, dedicated support).

2) Trial mapping: For a 14-day trial consider "14-day free evaluation (no credit card) — automatic conversion to paid unless cancelled" only if the account owner explicitly opts in per their compliance needs. More common is a trial entitlement SKU that grants trial capacity and expires — then move to paid SKU via Private Offer or checkout. We'll provide a sample entitlement wording below.

3) Attachments: I added a pricing column to your matrix (attached) with recommended meter names and example unit windows.

Action: I can draft the marketplace pricing snippet and a suggested entitlement CTA for the product page. Who wants to own the AMI checklist?

Quick AMI readiness checklist from infra side — high-level (I can turn this into a one-page doc):
- Required tags: aws:marketplace-seller-id, Version, BuildDate, Region
- Boot smoke tests: instance boots to login prompt within 90s, service agent starts on systemd, health endpoint responds (200)
- Networking: only required ports open, no hardcoded external creds, documented outbound endpoints for telemetry
- Packaging: compressed AMI image name matches listing, bootstrap script idempotent
- Security: minimal attack surface, latest OS patches, verified kernel modules

Note on BYO vs AMI: If they plan BYO, we need clear instructions for agent install + entitlement verification. If they want us to verify the AMI before publishing, we can run a quick boot/agent smoke on our side (I estimate ~2 hours).

I attached a short "ami-boot-checklist.pdf" and included three quick command snippets in the doc that they can run.

Kim

Hi team — thanks for the detailed notes. Short answers: 
1) Trial entitlements: We support non-billable entitlement SKUs that can be time-limited; those are surfaced as "Free trial" on the product page if configured as such. Private Offers can include trial coupons but visibility varies by buyer flow — recommend explicit CTA copy to avoid confusion.
2) AMI validation: Our automated checks require the seller-id tag and image name to match the listing metadata. Boot checks only fail if the image doesn't reach the init stage or if required services are missing. We can share the full validation spec (link below).

Link: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/ami-validation-specs

If helpful, we can set up a preflight validation run for DataForge — reply with AMI id and a preferred test window.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Onboarding
